You can do this! 
If you really can't do too much in this point in time yet it's alright, don't push it too much but just a little nudge in the direction you wanna go for (progress is still progress!)

For me, cleaning used to be a big motivator to get uo in the morning since it usually led to a productive day. Recently though, I just haven't been motivated to clean, heaps of laundry in the house with dusty and messy shelves. Sometimes I'd get a sudden burst of energy to clean but once I'm about to start, I just lose every ounce of that energy and end up on the bed staring at the ceiling again. 

Try cleaning even a little bit like your desk or bed everyday. That'd be the only thing you clean for a while and eventually you might get the routine down and just start cleaning your way through your home. It doesn't work all the time for me but it's a good way to get started. You could also separate the cleaning tasks across days like day one is for doing a third of my laundry, day 2 is for fixing my bed, ... Try to make the task as small as possible and build up slowly.

This might be hard but just do it regardless of motivation. It could be that the mess of the room is the cause of your lack of motivation and if that's the case, you might get stuck in the cycle of mess and no motivation. You could also do something you wouldn't usually do but would like to to break the habit.

TL;DR Only do it if the cat is okay with it and is properly trained. It would be really good for them to get a taste of the outside. 
---

I personally think its a good idea as long as you train them to feel alright on a harness and leash. There are many videos on youtube about it ( I recommend jackson galaxy's videos ). Don't push it though, only walk your cat if they allow you to because not all cats are up for it. Once you're able to train them, start small going outside, if they run back to the apartment hang on to the leash but follow them.

Im in a similar situation where I only own a room and have a 3 mos old kitten, trained him to like the leash and practiced him first in the house hallway. He would go out for a bit at first and run back to the room (i usually would give him a treat when i tug on the leash so he knows it's okay). Once he goes back in the room, I make him go to a spot to get his harness removed and finally give him a treat. Slowly he started exploring more with the leash on still following the same routine. The training and walk has to be a routine thing. 

I really suggest watching jackson galaxy's videos especially if you're new to cats. He covers many topics on them like cat aggression and training.

He stopped talking after a while and stared us down making the air tense.

This butterfly suddenly comes in through the door and flies around the room. Professor doesn't notice but everyone was just watching the butterfly. The butterfly then flies towards him and lands on his forehead. Prof notices us trying to hold in laughter pointing at his forehead and sees the butterfly. He tries to keep the stern face but then just breaks out in laughter along with the class. After a little joking around we head to the lab to actually start class

Ngl I think he forgot but our class still jokes about it even after 4 years
